name: Can you build a single-family home on a small or narrow lot in Glendale or Pasadena?

mainEntity.name: Can a single-family home be built on a small, narrow, or irregular lot in Glendale or Pasadena?
mainEntity.text: Can a single-family home be built on a small, narrow, or irregular lot in Glendale or Pasadena?

acceptedAnswer.text: Building on a small, narrow, or irregular lot is possible, but it usually requires more design creativity and more upfront due diligence. Setbacks, lot coverage rules, easements, access requirements, and utility locations can reduce the actual buildable area far below the lot size. In cities like Glendale and Pasadena, the layout may need to be optimized around driveway access, privacy, light, and circulation rather than a conventional rectangular plan. A good architect and builder should evaluate the site before the design is finalized so there are no surprises later in plan check. Owners should also confirm whether a garage, second story, or specific massing approach is realistically allowed. The key is to determine what fits the lot legally and functionally before committing to a concept.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but the lot shape, setbacks, access, and utility placement may limit the home’s footprint and design. Narrow or irregular lots often require more careful planning, creative floor plans, and early review of zoning, easements, and buildable area.
